flags.observation: "agreed to a ninety-nine-year WTC lease signed" fuses two card facts into broken grammar; the privatization agreement disappears.
Trailing "empire" dangles with no grammatical anchor; a listener cannot parse it as a claim.
"paid back initial equity and control" makes control something the Port Authority paid back, distorting the card.
"specific and commercial" is a fragment without meaning; the card's first-on-the-planet claim is lost.
"firm formerly chaired by CIA" says the agency chaired the firm; the card names a person, the CIA's number three.
"admitted knowing a DOD staffer; cashed out a day before" leaves the subject ambiguous; it reads as if Baer cashed out.
"But the SEC asks" plus "advanced knowledge" inverts the card: the SEC concluded nothing happened; the question belongs to the card voice.
"So the double policy" only restates the card name; no therefore or twist grows from the previous card.
"But" openers at beats 7 and 16 are nine lines apart; "Yet" at 13 and 22 also nine; the So/But/Yet rotation feels mechanical.
Openers like "Trading:", "Audit:", "Recovered:" are labels; almost no artworkPrompt image words appear anywhere (tip five); cards show no want or grudge.
122 characters with opener; "first rule Follow the Money rejected; little significance" is not sayable in one breath.
Outro turn is thin: "the receipts have names" closes the ledger image but adds little provocation; the frame barely carries the kayfabe concept.
